source: authored in-tree for the AEAT record-batch reader
notes: Hand-authored VERI*FACTU submission, fictional data, structured after aeat-verifactu-SuministroInformacion.xsd. Authored rather than taken from a captured sample because every real specimen available fails to DISCRIMINATE at least one trap, and a specimen that would pass with the defect present proves nothing. Four properties are deliberate. (1) MIXED BATCH: one RegFactuSistemaFacturacion carries a RegistroAlta AND a RegistroAnulacion, which the schema permits via a choice repeated to maxOccurs=1000 and which no captured sample shows; a reader classifying per FILE rather than per RECORD gets one of them wrong. (2) THREE DISTINCT NombreRazon VALUES: Cabecera/ObligadoEmision is 'OBLIGADO Cabecera SL', Destinatarios/IDDestinatario is 'DESTINATARIO Nacional SA', and SistemaInformatico -- the BILLING SOFTWARE VENDOR, never a party -- is 'PROVEEDOR Software SL', while the issuer's own NombreRazonEmisor is 'EMISOR Verdadero SL'. All four differ, so a namespace-agnostic descendant walk for the local name NombreRazon reports a wrong value whichever one it lands on. The bundled josemmo specimen cannot be used for this: there SistemaInformatico/NombreRazon is byte-identical to NombreRazonEmisor and carries the same NIF, so a loose walk returns the CORRECT answer and the test would certify the bug as working. (3) ENCADENAMIENTO DECOY ON BOTH RECORDS: the alta's RegistroAnterior names FA/2026-0043 while the alta itself is FA/2026-0044, and the anulacion's RegistroAnterior names FA/2026-0044 while it cancels FA/2026-0041 -- so an identity lookup that is not scoped to the record's own IDFactura reports the hash-chain predecessor instead of the subject, and the anulacion case makes that visible because the two differ. (4) TWO RECIPIENTS, ONE FOREIGN: one stated by NIF and one by IDOtro carrying CodigoPais/IDType/ID, so the multi-recipient cardinality and the alternative identifier scheme are both exercised; note the anulacion's IDFactura uses the -Anulada element spellings, which differ from a registration's.
